english: Partizip I for simultaneous action
note: describes what the subject is doing at the same time as the main action — a compact stand-in for a während-clause.

examples.de: Lächelnd verließ sie den Raum.
examples.en: Smiling, she left the room.

english: Partizip II for passive meaning
note: signals that something was done TO the subject — recoverable as a weil/da-clause with a passive verb.

examples.de: Von allen bewundert, genoss er seinen Erfolg.
examples.en: Admired by everyone, he enjoyed his success.

german: gleiches Subjekt in Haupt- und Partizipialsatz
english: the participial phrase's implied subject must match the main clause's subject
note: the single most important rule here — whoever or whatever the participle describes has to be the same as the main clause's grammatical subject.

examples.de: Auf die Frage angesprochen, antwortete sie ruhig.
examples.en: Asked about the question, she answered calmly.

german: Komma trennt die Partizipialphrase vom Hauptsatz
english: a comma separates the participial phrase from the main clause
note: whether the phrase opens or closes the sentence, a comma always marks the boundary — just like a subordinate clause would.

examples.de: Erschöpft von der langen Reise, schlief er sofort ein.
examples.en: Exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately.

english: unpacking into a temporal clause (als/nachdem)
note: a Partizip-II phrase from a sein-verb often unpacks into a nachdem-clause with the Plusquamperfekt.

examples.de: In Berlin angekommen, suchte sie sofort ein Hotel. = Nachdem sie in Berlin angekommen war, suchte sie sofort ein Hotel.
examples.en: Having arrived in Berlin, she immediately looked for a hotel.

english: unpacking into a causal clause (weil/da)
note: when the participial phrase gives a reason rather than just a time, weil or da is the natural unpacking.

examples.de: Erschöpft von der langen Reise, schlief er sofort ein. = Weil er von der langen Reise erschöpft war, schlief er sofort ein.
examples.en: Exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately.

german: Auf die Frage angesprochen, antwortete sie ruhig
english: Asked about the question, she answered calmly — example
note: a passive-flavored Partizip II phrase — she is the one being addressed, and also the main clause's subject.

examples.de: Auf die Frage angesprochen, antwortete sie ruhig.
examples.en: Asked about the question, she answered calmly.

german: Erschöpft von der langen Reise, schlief er sofort ein
english: Exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately — example
note: a causal reading is the most natural one here, even though there's no explicit weil.

examples.de: Erschöpft von der langen Reise, schlief er sofort ein.
examples.en: Exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately.

german: In Berlin angekommen, suchte sie sofort ein Hotel
english: Having arrived in Berlin, she immediately looked for a hotel — example
note: a completed-before-the-main-action reading, since ankommen is a sein-verb — like a compressed nachdem-clause.

examples.de: In Berlin angekommen, suchte sie sofort ein Hotel.
examples.en: Having arrived in Berlin, she immediately looked for a hotel.

english: Smiling, she left the room — example
note: a single-word Partizip I acting as a manner adverbial — the simplest form of this construction.

examples.de: Lächelnd verließ sie den Raum.
examples.en: Smiling, she left the room.

german: Von allen bewundert, genoss er seinen Erfolg
english: Admired by everyone, he enjoyed his success — example
note: von allen names the agent, just like in a full passive sentence.

examples.de: Von allen bewundert, genoss er seinen Erfolg.
examples.en: Admired by everyone, he enjoyed his success.

german: Überzeugt von ihrem Plan, begann sie sofort mit der Umsetzung
english: Convinced of her plan, she immediately began implementing it — example
note: überzeugt von + Dat behaves the same way as bewundert von — a passive-flavored Partizip II opener.

examples.de: Überzeugt von ihrem Plan, begann sie sofort mit der Umsetzung.
examples.en: Convinced of her plan, she immediately began implementing it.

english: to address, bring up (a topic)
note: separable — the Partizip II angesprochen is what appears in Auf die Frage angesprochen, …

examples.de: Sie wurde auf die Frage angesprochen und antwortete ruhig.
examples.en: She was addressed about the question and answered calmly.

english: to exhaust
note: inseparable, no ge- (erschöpft) — the source of the adjective/participle erschöpft.

examples.de: Die lange Reise hat ihn völlig erschöpft.
examples.en: The long journey completely exhausted him.

english: to smile
note: a plain, regular verb — its Partizip I lächelnd is the classic simultaneous-action example.

examples.de: Sie lächelte, als sie den Raum verließ.
examples.en: She smiled as she left the room.

english: to admire
note: inseparable, no ge- (bewundert) — the source of the participial phrase von allen bewundert.

examples.de: Alle bewunderten seinen Erfolg.
examples.en: Everyone admired his success.

english: to convince
note: inseparable, no ge- (überzeugt) — the source of überzeugt von as a participial opener.

examples.de: Ihr Plan hat das ganze Team überzeugt.
examples.en: Her plan convinced the whole team.

english: a comparison: a full nachdem-clause vs. the reduced participial phrase
note: the participial phrase is shorter and more literary; the nachdem-clause is more explicit and easier to produce under pressure.

examples.de: Nachdem sie in Berlin angekommen war, suchte sie ein Hotel. / In Berlin angekommen, suchte sie ein Hotel.
examples.en: After she had arrived in Berlin, she looked for a hotel. / Having arrived in Berlin, she looked for a hotel.

english: a comparison: a full weil-clause vs. the reduced participial phrase
note: German often leaves the causal connection implicit in the participial version — the reader has to infer weil/da from context.

examples.de: Weil er von der langen Reise erschöpft war, schlief er sofort ein. / Erschöpft von der langen Reise, schlief er sofort ein.
examples.en: Because he was exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately. / Exhausted from the long journey, he fell asleep immediately.

english: a comparison: a full während-clause vs. the reduced participial phrase
note: Partizip I phrases almost always correspond to a während-clause describing simultaneous action.

examples.de: Während sie lächelte, verließ sie den Raum. / Lächelnd verließ sie den Raum.
examples.en: While she smiled, she left the room. / Smiling, she left the room.

english: astonished
note: Partizip II of erstaunen used adjectivally — pairs with über + Akk in a participial opener.

examples.de: Erstaunt über die Nachricht, sagte sie zunächst nichts.
examples.en: Astonished by the news, she said nothing at first.

english: driven, motivated
note: Partizip II of treiben used adjectivally — pairs with von + Dat naming what drives the subject.

examples.de: Getrieben von Ehrgeiz, arbeitete er Tag und Nacht.
examples.en: Driven by ambition, he worked day and night.

english: surrounded
note: Partizip II of umgeben used adjectivally — pairs with von + Dat naming what surrounds the subject.

examples.de: Umgeben von Journalisten, verließ er das Gerichtsgebäude.
examples.en: Surrounded by journalists, he left the courthouse.

english: accompanied
note: Partizip II of begleiten used adjectivally — pairs with von + Dat naming who accompanies the subject.

examples.de: Begleitet von ihrem Anwalt, betrat sie den Gerichtssaal.
examples.en: Accompanied by her lawyer, she entered the courtroom.

german: Erstaunt über die Nachricht, sagte sie zunächst nichts
english: Astonished by the news, she said nothing at first — example
note: the participle's implied cause (the news) doesn't have to be the main clause's subject — sie is.

examples.de: Erstaunt über die Nachricht, sagte sie zunächst nichts.
examples.en: Astonished by the news, she said nothing at first.

german: Getrieben von Ehrgeiz, arbeitete er Tag und Nacht
english: Driven by ambition, he worked day and night — example
note: a vivid, almost literary way to explain someone's motivation without a plain weil-clause.

examples.de: Getrieben von Ehrgeiz, arbeitete er Tag und Nacht.
examples.en: Driven by ambition, he worked day and night.

german: Umgeben von Journalisten, verließ er das Gerichtsgebäude
english: Surrounded by journalists, he left the courthouse — example
note: a common construction in news writing, setting a scene efficiently before the main action.

examples.de: Umgeben von Journalisten, verließ er das Gerichtsgebäude.
examples.en: Surrounded by journalists, he left the courthouse.

german: Begleitet von ihrem Anwalt, betrat sie den Gerichtssaal
english: Accompanied by her lawyer, she entered the courtroom — example
note: another news-style scene-setter, very close in structure to the umgeben example.

examples.de: Begleitet von ihrem Anwalt, betrat sie den Gerichtssaal.
examples.en: Accompanied by her lawyer, she entered the courtroom.
